objective: Challenge SG037 trend interpretation with a differently constructed estimator. Preserve disagreement as unresolved (not proof of false decision) and measure extra abstentions against actual error prevention.
baseline: SG037 identical generator, predecision gate, 20-sample monitors and 20-sample confirmation window, unchanged.
estimator_A: Median of pairwise slopes among consecutive 10-sample bin medians, reject if |s|<.0018, confirm if |s|>.0032, else unresolved.
estimator_B: Median of first floor(n/3) observations rounded down to a multiple of 10 versus median of last equal-sized window, divided by distance between window centers (n-w); thresholds inherited from estimator A.
challenge: At early SG037 candidate commitment, require second estimator classification to equal candidate primary classification, else discard candidate and continue. At final 240, if a shift alarm latched and estimators disagree, record unresolved. No change to frozen SG037 predecision gate or shift monitor.

pilot.note: Pilot-inspected: second estimator caused ten additional abstentions and did not fix one wrong decision. This is a disclosed negative pilot, not holdout.

limitations: Two estimators analyze same data and share signal-model assumptions, not independent source ancestry.
Abstention may increase; disagreement is not necessarily error.
Synthetic scenarios, not real-world proof of general reliability.
